input.quote: 12.3 Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service, engaging any supplier, hiring any person who responds to general recruitment, or conducting business in any field or territory. Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding us, which meets the preferred position. Section 12.3 affirmatively preserves our freedom to develop, acquire, buy, build, sell, engage other suppliers, and operate in any field or territory, and records that we have given no non-compete commitment — language that benefits us and should be retained. Searches for competing-product, field-of-use, and territory restrictions returned nothing adverse: Section 13.4 contains only ordinary acceptable-use limits (no reverse engineering, no interference with the Services, no unlawful use), which are not competitive restraints, and Section 24.2's competitor language binds Vendor's assignment rights in our favour. Section 2.2's sole-and-exclusive-provider commitment is an exclusivity/minimum-source term addressed under the EXCLUSIVITY rule (and is in any event contradicted by Section 12.3), so we do not flag the same commercial term twice here. No redline required.
